summary: Madera County lookout on Potter Ridge: a 1905 wood cabin, a CCC-era tower dated 1934 or 1932 by sources, retired after 1994 and not open to the public today.

facts.design: 20-foot H-beam steel tower with a C-3(L) cab installed in 1952; the 1932 tower carried an L-4 or 4AR cab
facts.status_note: Still standing but retired from fire detection after the 1994 season; a 2008 photo showed extreme disrepair and a 2025-26 state request sought funds for preliminary repair plans.

access.note: About 4.5 miles from the paved road, behind locked gates; the register says it is not readily accessible to the public. Microwave dishes and radio vaults and towers are at the site.

visit.trail_note: Behind locked gates about 4.5 miles from the paved road; not open to visitors.

facts.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection (now CAL FIRE); the register ties the lookout to the Sierra National Forest

events.note: Original lookout on the site, a wood cabin design.
Staffed through the 1909 season; described as the first continually staffed lookout in the Sierra National Forest.
Replaced with a 20-foot H-beam steel tower carrying an L-4 or 4AR cab. Conflicts with the register's 1934 build date.
Register says the Civilian Conservation Corps constructed the tower and cab for the Sierra National Forest.
Utility room (Cook's Quarters) added below the cab by CDF; cab replaced with the current C-3(L) cab.
June 1968 break-in reported in the Madera Tribune; walkie-talkie, binoculars, blankets and gasoline taken.
Retired from active service after the end of the 1994 fire season.
Last photo seen by the fire-lookouts.org author, showing the tower in extreme disrepair.
CAL FIRE budget request (fiscal year 2025-26) for $587,000 of preliminary plans for the joint Penon Blanco and Deadwood Peak repair project; total estimated project cost $11,434,000.

corrections.proposed: 20-foot H-beam steel tower with a C-3(L) cab (installed 1952)
corrections.why: fire-lookouts.org says the L-4 or 4AR cab was the 1932 cab and was replaced by the current C-3(L) cab in 1952.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register dates the CCC-built tower and cab to 1934, with a 1952 addition. fire-lookouts.org says a steel tower replaced the earlier structure in 1932. The story gives both and keeps the register date as the headline build year.

The register places the lookout in the Sierra National Forest with CDF administration. fire-lookouts.org says the tower stands on private leased land outside the forest boundary. The story reports both accounts.

notes_for_editor: Build year conflicts (1932 steel tower per fire-lookouts.org vs 1934 CCC tower per NHLR); both are reported. The brief's L-4 design is only the 1932 cab; current cab is C-3(L). The brief's NHLR registration date (2019-12-23) does not appear in the cached register text, so no nhlr_registered event was added. A Deadwood Lookout Rec Cabin in Idaho (destinationwild.com) is a different tower and was excluded. The EverybodyWiki article is flagged as AI-generated and was not used. No notable fires and no recreation.gov listing found for the California tower. Access level set to restricted based on the register text; no rental program found.
